<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/plugins/development.mdx`  _(via outDir (symbol, a field of const object browserConfig))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9a1e93f437ac1d9c20042912acfa39bb434d938` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ad237dd74d159fb66f634a785296e89500801275` — the merge of head `5a40a4207564c9e7f5ef4690db2fce2ab5ff122b` into base `f9a1e93f437ac1d9c20042912acfa39bb434d938`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ad237dd74d159fb66f634a785296e89500801275 && git checkout ad237dd74d159fb66f634a785296e89500801275
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f9a1e93f437ac1d9c20042912acfa39bb434d938 5a40a4207564c9e7f5ef4690db2fce2ab5ff122b && git checkout -B drift-repro f9a1e93f437ac1d9c20042912acfa39bb434d938 && git merge --no-ff 5a40a4207564c9e7f5ef4690db2fce2ab5ff122b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9a1e93f437ac1d9c20042912acfa39bb434d938
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f9a1e93f437ac1d9c20042912acfa39bb434d938` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #8133 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-25T05:13Z · head `5a40a42075` · report `6393762205` (on #8133; cloud session `session_01Q3XCv7AXcUSSD479Vt1LXy`) · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. `dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` over the 4 paths: no path-derived mandate. The diff reaches nothing under `packages/spec/src/**`, so per the claim no contract review is owed and `needs:contract-review` is not added.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #8133`, title `build(spec):`. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Ruling-ref: none` are line-initial in the body and in the changeset (`@objectstack/spec` `patch`). 4 files, +220/−48. `check-governed-merges --pr 25748` (dev's run): 0 of 4 paths governed, 268 changed lines.
2. **The card's direction, measured on the diff.** The reopen `6370298049` names direction A: shared chunks for the ESM and browser builds, with the `exports` map unchanged.
   - `jsConfig` builds all 24 outputs (19 ordinary plus 5 `dist/browser/*`) as one esbuild graph with `splitting: true`.
   - `mainConfig` stays per-entry and is now read only by the DTS pass and `pure-schema-construction.test.ts`. The DTS options hash is identical at BASE and HEAD.
   - **The claim's mechanism lead was corrected by measurement.** A bare `splitting: true` made `./shared` and `./migrations` link the chunk that imports `pg-connection-string`, the #11072 class that `check:browser-reachable-entries` rule 2 refuses. That happens because esbuild chunks by file-level reachability. The dev followed the measurement.
   - **How the fix works.** The browser swap applies graph-wide, and only the modules that reach the seam get a node-side copy.
   - **How the node-side set is found.** It is computed per build by a metafile pre-pass, not kept as a list, and the build refuses when the seam disappears. Read in the diff:
     - The swap stands aside only for resolutions carrying `pluginData.nodeSide`.
     - Node-side imports resolve through `build.resolve` and stay on the node side only when their target is in the measured set.
     - Every other import goes back to the shared `file` namespace.
3. **Results against the card's done-when.**
   - `defineConnector` from the root is `defineConnector` from `/integration`, in both ESM and CJS: false → **true**.
   - `FieldSchema` is defined in 14 `.mjs` files → **1**.
   - `dist` shrinks from 123.5M to **53.5M**.
   - The `exports` map and the declaration file set are unchanged.
   - The objectui import experiment (256 value imports, gzip 9) drops from 1,628.4 KB to **603.6 KB**.
   - The card's first done-when, objectui `Bundle Analysis` `vendor-objectstack` on a pin carrying this change, is **NOT MEASURED** here, and the PR says so. It is carried as a paired objectui card, below.
4. **Gates.**
   - `ci-failure --pr 25748` on `5a40a42075`: 43 check-runs. The only failure so far is `Spec property liveness`, the main-red `translation/flows.screens` (#25742, fix in flight on this seat). It is not this diff: no ledger, no `service-automation` file and nothing under `src/` is touched. `Test Core` takes the same red through `check-liveness.test.ts` until the base carries #25742's fix.
   - Local at `19a8800a` (before the base merge):
     - root `pnpm test`: 152/152 tasks, every package reading spec through `dist`
     - dogfood battery: 295 files / 2520 tests
     - cli: 500 files / 6291 tests
     - `pnpm build`: 76/76 tasks
     - all 72 derived commands: exit 0
   - At `5a40a420`: 71/72 exit 0, the one exit 1 being `check:liveness` (main-red). `--ran`: 0 NOT-MEASURED. All dist-reading gates exit 0: `check:browser-reachable-entries`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`, `check:published-files`.
   - **Ablations, each predicted then observed, each restored blob-identical:**
     - A1 (browser swap off): rule 2 red, 14 problems.
     - A2 (node-side twinning off): `POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED`.
     - A3 (seam regex dead): the build refuses in both ESM and CJS.
5. **Producers.**
   - **objectui** `a3c0da9`: 3 `@objectstack/spec/dist/index.*` strings, all regex probe inputs in tests, not imports. `objectstack-pin.mjs` hard-links the whole package tree, so the chunks travel with it.
   - **HotCRM** `a4b3560`: 0 deep imports.
   - Chunk names are unstable by design, and the changeset tells consumers to import only through the `exports` map.
6. **Open questions.**
   - (1) Three comments under `packages/spec/src/**` now misdescribe the layout: `src/index.ts:73`, `src/conversions/registry.ts:18144`, and `src/api/package-api-assembled.zod.ts:40`, which renders into generated docs. **A**: the seat files one comment-only follow-up card at this PR's merge. `src/**` stays out of this PR so its tier stays honest.
   - (2) Under Node, 5 metadata-collection exports still differ between the root and `/shared`. Under `browser` they are one object. **A**: no consumer is measured comparing them by identity. Making them one object would mean an `exports`-map change or a `src` split, and nobody ruled either.
   - (3) CJS also takes shared chunks. **A**: the chunk graph has 0 cycles (1,158 CJS edges), and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` would fail loudly on a cyclic future. The reopen left CJS "judged on its own", and this is that judgement, with evidence.
7. **Deviations accepted.**
   - `packages/spec/README.md` (published) is outside the claim's file surface. Its sentence "Each entry is a self-contained bundle" becomes false with this change, so correcting it in the same PR is in kind.
   - The changeset quotes 602.9 KB (pre-merge head) where the body's HEAD reading is 603.6 KB. Both are true readings on different trees. Acceptance note, no carrier.
   - `mcp_calls` 0. Relay writes 2.
8. **Landing.**
   - The base merge comes once #25742's fix is in `main`.
   - When every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.
   - At merge, the seat files two paired cards:
     - **objectui**: the pin move that measures `vendor-objectstack` under `Bundle Analysis`, names the number, and re-baselines the eager-closure ceilings once. This is the card's own done-when.
     - **objectstack**: (1)'s comment-only follow-up.
